sources.analysis: ACI 209R-92 Chapter 2: the creep and shrinkage of the members in the analysis
sources.phased: ACI 209R-92 Sec 2.2: the age at loading of each storey (construction sequence: SAEngine practice)
sources.effects: ASCE 7-22 Sec 2.3.4 and ACI 318-19 Sec 5.3.6: self-straining effects of creep and shrinkage
sources.creepFigure: ACI 209R-92 Eqs 2-11 to 2-14, 2-21: loading age (moist cured), relative humidity and volume-to-surface factors
sources.creepDevelopment: ACI 209R-92 Eq 2-8: the time-ratio of creep
sources.thickness: ACI 209R-92 Eqs 2-14 and 2-21: volume-to-surface ratio V/S (= half the effective thickness 2A/u)

sources.shrinkageFigure: ACI 209R-92 Table 2.5.3 and Eqs 2-15, 2-22: curing, relative humidity and volume-to-surface factors

creep.note: Standard conditions for the slump, fines and air factors (Eqs 2-17 to 2-19 at 1.0): otherFactor 1.0, SAEngine practice. The volume-to-surface ratio V/S is half the effective thickness 2A/u. Moist curing (the steam-cured loading age factor 1.13 t^-0.094 is not used).

shrinkage.note: Moist curing (f = 35 days); the curing factor interpolated linearly between the tabulated days. Slump, fines, cement content and air factors at 1.0 (standard conditions): SAEngine practice.

exposure.source: SAEngine practice (ACI 209R-92 takes the project's ambient relative humidity)
exposure.note: ACI 209R-92 gives no indoor and outdoor humidities: 50 % indoors and 70 % outdoors are SAEngine's defaults; enter the project's relative humidity to replace them.

strengthGain.source: ACI 209R-92 Eq 2-1 and Table 2.2.1: moist-cured concrete with Type I cement

ageing.source: SAEngine practice: the usual ageing coefficient of the age-adjusted effective modulus method
ageing.note: ACI 209R-92 does not tabulate χ; 0.8 is the usual value for loads applied at once.

analysis.note: The steel restrains the creep and shrinkage by the age-adjusted effective modulus.
